title: TP/SL order ids lose precision: Number.parseInt truncates uint256 ids above 2^53 in GET/DELETE
reasoning: Order creation stores the on-chain uint256 order id as a decimal string (onchainOrderId = eventArgs.orderId.toString(), line 228), but GET /orders/:id and DELETE /orders/:id convert the path param with Number.parseInt. Any id >= 2^53 (9007199254740993) is rounded to the nearest double, so lookups and cancellations target a different (or non-existent) id — a cancel could silently no-op or hit the wrong row. Additionally parseInt silently accepts malformed input like "1.5" (→ 1), returning the wrong order instead of 400. On-chain order ids are uint256 and can legitimately exceed 2^53.
reproduction: Create an order whose OrderCreated event carries orderId 9007199254740993, then GET /api/v1/tp-sl/orders/9007199254740993 — the parsed id becomes 9007199254740992 and the lookup misses.
recommendation: Validate the param with /^\d+$/ and pass the id as a string through to getOrder/cancelOrder, keeping ids as strings end-to-end (the service already stores the string form).
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tp-sl route tests exist in the included test set; only price-guard is tested.
suggestedRegressionTest: Unit/integration test that a large id (e.g., 9007199254740993) round-trips through getOrder/cancelOrder without precision loss, and that "1.5" is rejected with 400.
minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/routes/tp-sl.ts GET/DELETE handlers plus TpSlService signatures to accept string ids.
